For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\), the index
\[
 \widehat k_m=
 \min\left\{k\ge1:
 \widehat w_m^+(C_k)
 \le \inf_{j\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_j)+\varepsilon_m
 \right\}
\]
is finite and pilot-measurable.  Hence \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}\) is a measurable class of rank \(r_\Omega\) in the note's quotient of Zhao's published carrier and satisfies
\[
 \widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
 \le
 \inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\]
The selector is rank two exactly when rank two is achievable.  No full-carrier minimizer or zero-tolerance selector is used.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix the design.  Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  For each \(e\in\{L,U\}\), the empirical endpoint covariance is attained by the comonotone or antimonotone quantile coupling \(\widehat H_e\) of the two empirical marginals.  If
\[
\mathcal Y=(Y_1(1),\ldots,Y_n(1),-Y_1(0),\ldots,-Y_n(0))^{\top}
\]
under \(\widehat H_e^{\otimes n}\), the endpoint construction gives
\[
\widehat Q_e=\mathbb E_{\widehat H_e^{\otimes n}}(\mathcal Y\mathcal Y^{\top})\succeq0.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\widehat A_e
=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}\widehat Q_e\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}
\succeq0.
\tag{2}
\]
For every carrier class, the empirical endpoint residual can therefore be written as
\[
\widehat\ell_{B,e}^+
=\widehat h_e-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_B\widehat A_e),
\qquad e\in\{L,U\},
\tag{3}
\]
where \(\widehat h_e=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Q_e)\) is independent of \(B\).

We next verify that the sequence \((C_k)\) is nonempty and dense in the objective values on the maximal-rank stratum.  If \(r_\Omega=2\), choose any rank-two representative.  Positive definiteness of \(B^{\top}\Omega B\) is open.  Rational directions are dense in every signed pivot chart, and normalization is continuous away from zero.  Hence rational-support rank-two classes exist, and every rank-two class is the limit of a subsequence of \((C_k)\).  On this fixed-rank stratum the projector, and therefore (3), is continuous.

If \(r_\Omega=1\), let \([B]_+\) have rank one.  At least one arm column, say the arm indexed by \(a\), has a nonzero image
\[
z_a=\Omega^{1/2}B_ae_a\ne0.
\]
Choose nonzero rational vectors \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^n\) converging to that arm direction.  Continuity makes their corresponding images nonzero for all sufficiently large \(j\).  Form a block class with the normalized rational vector in arm \(a\) and the other arm equal to zero.  Its rank is one, because \(r_\Omega=1\) rules out rank two.  The resulting one-dimensional projectors converge to the projector onto \(\operatorname{span}(z_a)=\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\).  These rational-support classes occur in \((C_k)\), so their values in (3) converge to the value at \(B\).  If \(r_\Omega=0\), every attainable projector is zero and the repeated zero class prescribed in the definition is nonempty and has every carrier value.

It remains to compare lower-rank classes with the maximal-rank enumeration.  Fix \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\).  By the corrected approximation clause of \(\texttt{lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction}\), there are maximal-rank classes \([B_j]_+\) and a projector \(P_\infty\) such that
\[
P_{B_j}\longrightarrow P_\infty,
\qquad P_\infty-P_B\succeq0.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) and trace monotonicity imply
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}\widehat w_m^+(B_j)
\le \widehat w_m^+(B).
\tag{5}
\]
For \(r_\Omega=2\), approximate each fixed \(B_j\) by an enumerated rational-support rank-two class; for \(r_\Omega=1\), use the rational one-arm approximation just proved; and for \(r_\Omega=0\), use the zero class.  Thus for every \(\delta>0\) some \(C_k\) satisfies
\[
\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\widehat w_m^+(B)+\delta.
\tag{6}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(k\), then over \([B]_+\), and finally letting \(\delta\downarrow0\) proves
\[
\inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k)
\le\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B).
\tag{7}
\]
The reverse inequality follows because every \(C_k\) is a carrier class.  This proves equality of the infima without continuity across rank changes or attainment of the full-carrier infimum.

For measurability, fix \(k\).  Empirical means and variances are measurable functions of the pilot observations, and the empirical quantile-coupling cross moments are finite functions of order statistics.  Since \(C_k\), its rank, and its pseudoinverse are fixed by the design,
\[
X_k:=\widehat w_m^+(C_k)
\]
is pilot-measurable.  Therefore \(\rho_m=\inf_{j\ge1}X_j\) is measurable.  Strict positivity and finiteness of \(\varepsilon_m\) make the qualifying set nonempty by the definition of an infimum.  Moreover,
\[
\{\widehat k_m=k\}
=\{X_k\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\}
\cap\bigcap_{j<k}\{X_j>\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\},
\tag{8}
\]
so \(\widehat k_m\) is measurable.  The countable-valued selector \(C_{\widehat k_m}\) is consequently measurable, has rank \(r_\Omega\), and satisfies the stated positive-tolerance inequality.  Since \(r_\Omega=2\) exactly when a rank-two class is achievable, the final rank assertion follows. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, fix \(n\), form the two empirical endpoint matrices in def:pilot-plugin, and put
\[
 M_m=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
 \lVert \widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
As \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(M_m\to0\) almost surely under the pilot law \(P\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For arm \(a\), write \(F_{a,m_a}\) for the distribution function of \(\widehat F_a\).  For fixed rational \(t\in[0,1]\), the variables
\[
X_{j,a}(t)=\mathbf 1\{Y^P_{j,a}\le t\}
\]
are independent Bernoulli variables with mean \(F_a(t)\).  If \(X\) is Bernoulli with mean \(p\), then
\[
\mathbb E\exp\{\lambda(X-p)\}
=e^{-\lambda p}(1-p+pe^\lambda)\le e^{\lambda^2/8}.
\tag{1}
\]
To verify (1), the second derivative of \(\log(1-p+pe^\lambda)\) is the variance of a tilted Bernoulli variable and is at most \(1/4\), while that logarithm minus \(p\lambda\) and its first derivative vanish at zero.  Exponential Markov inequality, independence, and optimization of the exponential bound give, for \(s>0\),
\[
P\!\left(\left|F_{a,m_a}(t)-F_a(t)\right|>s\right)
\le2e^{-2m_as^2}.
\tag{2}
\]
For every rational \(s>0\), the right side is summable in \(m_a\).  The union bound and the tail-sum form of the Borel--Cantelli argument imply
\[
P\!\left(\limsup_{m_a\to\infty}
\{|F_{a,m_a}(t)-F_a(t)|>s\}\right)=0.
\tag{3}
\]
Intersecting the probability-one events in (3) over the countable rational pairs \((t,s)\) gives simultaneous convergence at every rational \(t\).

Fix an integer \(K\ge1\) and the rational grid \(x_j=j/K\).  Monotonicity of the two distribution functions implies, for \(y\in[x_j,x_{j+1}]\),
\[
|F_{a,m_a}(y)-F_a(y)|
\le
\max_{r\in\{j,j+1\}}|F_{a,m_a}(x_r)-F_a(x_r)|
+F_a(x_{j+1})-F_a(x_j).
\tag{4}
\]
Integrating (4), summing over \(j\), using convergence on the finite grid, and telescoping the last increments gives
\[
\limsup_{m_a\to\infty}
\int_0^1|F_{a,m_a}(y)-F_a(y)|\,dy\le K^{-1}
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{5}
\]
Letting \(K\to\infty\) proves that the integral in (5) converges to zero.

For distribution functions \(R,S\) on \([0,1]\), the one-dimensional quantile identity
\[
\int_0^1|R^{-1}(u)-S^{-1}(u)|\,du
=\int_0^1|R(y)-S(y)|\,dy
\tag{6}
\]
follows by the layer-cake representation and Tonelli's theorem.  Equations (5)--(6) show
\[
\int_0^1|\widehat F_a^{-1}(u)-F_a^{-1}(u)|\,du
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely},
\qquad a\in\{1,0\}.
\tag{7}
\]
The bounded support in (4)--(7) is exactly the bounded-outcomes assumption.

The functions \(y\) and \(y^2\) are respectively one- and two-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\), so (7) gives convergence of the empirical means, second moments, and variances.  Moreover,
\[
|xy-x'y'|\le|x-x'|+|y-y'|
\qquad(x,x',y,y'\in[0,1]).
\tag{8}
\]
Applying (8) to both the comonotone and antimonotone quantile pairs proves almost-sure convergence of the two empirical cross moments and hence of both empirical covariance endpoints.

By the moment-matrix formula and the endpoint-matrix construction in the corrected pilot definition, every block of \(\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\) is a convergent scalar multiplying either \(I_n\) or \(\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\).  Because \(n\) is fixed,
\[
\lVert I_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=1,
\qquad
\lVert\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=n.
\tag{9}
\]
Therefore
\[
M_m=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely under }P.
\tag{10}
\]
The maximal-rank enumeration and first-qualifying selector in the corrected pilot definition do not enter this endpoint calculation, so the definition correction leaves the lemma unchanged. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity.  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, let \(\widehat w_m^+(B)\) and, for \(\varepsilon_m>0\), \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) be the distinct full-class empirical objective and measurable first-qualifying maximal-rank selector in def:pilot-plugin, and put
\[
d_m^+=\sup_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}|\widehat w_m^+(B)-w^+(B)|.
\]
As \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(d_m^+\to0\) almost surely and
\[
\left|\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\right|
\le d_m^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
For every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\),
\[
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\]
Consequently, if \(\varepsilon_m\to0\) almost surely, then
\[
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
The objective domain is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, and the measurable positive-tolerance selector has maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\), which is rank two exactly when rank two is achievable.  No exact selector at zero tolerance, cross-rank outer-argmin convergence, point convergence, or singular-rank feasible-estimator variance bridge is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Set
\[
M_m=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:bounded-unpaired-endpoint-strong-convergence}\), bounded outcomes and the unpaired-pilot sampling law imply
\[
M_m\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely as }m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty.
\tag{1}
\]
For the fixed design, exposure positivity gives
\[
\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}\pi_{i,a}>0.
\tag{2}
\]
The all-rank modulus in \(\texttt{lem:full-carrier-plugin-objective-regret-rate}\) therefore yields
\[
d_m^+
\le4\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}n^{-1}M_m
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{3}
\]

For arbitrary real-valued functions \(f\) and \(g\) on the same nonempty domain,
\[
|\inf f-\inf g|\le\sup|f-g|.
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, \(f\le g+\sup|f-g|\) gives one inequality after taking infima, and interchanging \(f\) and \(g\) gives the other.  The full carrier is nonempty because it contains the zero class.  Applying (4) to \(\widehat w_m^+\) and \(w^+\) on \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) proves
\[
\left|
\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)
-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
\right|
\le d_m^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{5}
\]

The corrected \(\texttt{def:pilot-plugin}\) enumerates rational-support classes of maximal achievable rank \(r_\Omega\), including the zero class when \(r_\Omega=0\).  By \(\texttt{lem:full-carrier-countable-measurable-selector}\), for every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\), the first qualifying index is finite and pilot-measurable and satisfies
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le
\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (6) with the definition of \(d_m^+\) twice gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
&\le\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)+d_m^+\\
&\le\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)
+\varepsilon_m+d_m^+\\
&\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Since \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) is the infimum of \(w^+\) over the same domain,
\[
0\le
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
\le2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (3) and (8) prove the final almost-sure convergence whenever \(\varepsilon_m\to0\) almost surely.

The selector lemma also gives \(\operatorname{rank}(S_{\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+})=r_\Omega\).  Thus the selector is rank two exactly when rank two is achievable; otherwise it is rank one or zero.  The proof uses only positive tolerances and infimum comparisons.  It assumes neither full-carrier attainment nor a zero-tolerance selector, and it establishes neither cross-rank outer-argmin convergence, point convergence, nor a feasible-estimator variance bridge at singular rank. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the two endpoint matrices obtained from the unpaired empirical marginals, put \(M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), and define
\[
C_n=n^{-2}\left[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*
+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
M_n=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad
C_n\le4\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}.
\]
More precisely, with
\[
A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\]
one has
\[
0\preceq A_B\preceq A_{\mathrm{HT}},
\qquad
\lVert A_B\rVert_*
\le\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}})
=\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\{1,0\}}\frac{1-\pi_{i,a}}{\pi_{i,a}}
\le2\underline\pi^{-1}n^{1+\beta}.
\]
The uniform plug-in inequalities are
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_nM_n,
\]
and, writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments,
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2M_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le2n^{-2}\sup_B\lVert A_B\rVert_*M_n
\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Hence the exact downstream premise
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0
\]
implies first-order plug-in accuracy in the explicit sense that the pilot expectations of both displayed uniform criterion errors are \(o(n^{-1})\).  The condition
\[
\frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty
\]
is sufficient.  Neither known exposure nor a dependency-neighborhood condition is used in this pilot-only matrix calculation.
statements.justification: This lemma gives a dependency-degree-free pilot sensitivity bound and preserves the exact first-order premise used by the feasible-estimator transfer theorem.
statements.gap: The positive-semidefinite projector order replaces the prior row-sparsity nuclear-norm estimate and yields the sufficient boundary \(\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}/n^{1+\beta}\to\infty\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(m=m_1\wedge m_0\), and let \(W_1\) denote the one-dimensional Wasserstein distance.  For probability laws \(R,S\) on \([0,1]\), the layer-cake identity followed by Fubini's theorem gives
\[
W_1(R,S)
=\int_0^1\lvert R^{-1}(u)-S^{-1}(u)\rvert\,du
=\int_0^1\lvert R(y)-S(y)\rvert\,dy.
\tag{1}
\]
For each arm \(a\), Jensen's inequality and the binomial variance formula give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_PW_1(\widehat F_a,F_a)
&=\int_0^1\mathbb E_P\lvert\widehat F_a(y)-F_a(y)\rvert\,dy\\
&\le\int_0^1\sqrt{\frac{F_a(y)\{1-F_a(y)\}}{m_a}}\,dy
\le\frac{1}{2\sqrt{m_a}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Because \(y\mapsto y\) and \(y\mapsto y^2\) are respectively one- and two-Lipschitz on \([0,1]\), equation (1) implies
\[
\lvert\widehat\mu_a-\mu_a\rvert\le W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a),
\qquad
\lvert\widehat\sigma_a^2-\sigma_a^2\rvert
\le4W_1(\widehat F_a,F_a).
\tag{3}
\]
For either the comonotone or countermonotone quantile product, the elementary inequality \(\lvert xy-x'y'\rvert\le\lvert x-x'\rvert+\lvert y-y'\rvert\) on \([0,1]^4\), together with (1), yields
\[
\lvert\widehat c_e-c_e\rvert
\le2\{W_1(\widehat F_1,F_1)+W_1(\widehat F_0,F_0)\},
\qquad e\in\{L,U\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Every block of \(\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\) is a linear combination of \(I_n\) and \(\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), with coefficients bounded by the errors in (3)--(4) and the analogous product-of-means error.  Since \(\lVert I_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=1\) and \(\lVert\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=n\), equations (2)--(4) imply, for a numerical constant \(K_M<\infty\),
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n
\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt m}.
\tag{5}
\]
This proves \(M_n=O_{L^1}(n/\sqrt m)\).

We next bound the deterministic sensitivity without using assignment dependency neighborhoods.  For \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), put \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\).  The regularity of this class makes \(Z_B^\top Z_B=B^\top\Omega B\) invertible, and
\[
P_B=Z_B(Z_B^\top Z_B)^{-1}Z_B^\top
\]
is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\).  Therefore \(0\preceq P_B\preceq I_{2n}\), and congruence by \(\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}\) gives
\[
0\preceq
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}P_B\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}
\preceq
\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}=A_{\mathrm{HT}}.
\tag{6}
\]
Both matrices in (6) are positive semidefinite, so their nuclear norms equal their traces.  Each coordinate of \(D\) is Bernoulli with mean \(\pi_{i,a}\), whence \(\Omega_{(i,a),(i,a)}=\pi_{i,a}(1-\pi_{i,a})\).  It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lVert A_B\rVert_*
&\le\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}})
=\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\{1,0\}}
\frac{\pi_{i,a}(1-\pi_{i,a})}{\pi_{i,a}^2}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\{1,0\}}
\frac{1-\pi_{i,a}}{\pi_{i,a}}
\le2\underline\pi^{-1}n^{1+\beta},
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
where the last inequality is ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate.  The same bound applies to \(\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_*\).  Hence
\[
C_n\le4\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}.
\tag{8}
\]

For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), the endpoint residual loss is \(n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{(A_{\mathrm{HT}}-A_B)Q(c_e)\}\), with the empirical analogue obtained by replacing \(Q(c_e)\) by \(\widehat Q_e\).  Trace duality and the inequality \(\lvert\max_e x_e-\max_e y_e\rvert\le\max_e\lvert x_e-y_e\rvert\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\lvert\widehat w(B)-w(B)\rvert
&\le n^{-2}\sup_B
\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}-A_B\rVert_*M_n\\
&\le C_nM_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]

It remains to compare the empirical zero-covariance matrix with an endpoint matrix.  Let \(\Delta_e=\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\) and \(d_e=\widehat c_e-c_e\).  The affine identities \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\) and \(\widehat Q_e=\widehat Q(0)-\widehat c_eE\) give
\[
\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)=\Delta_e+d_eE.
\tag{10}
\]
Choose a unit vector \(z\perp\mathbf1\), which exists because \(n\ge3\).  The cross block of \(\Delta_e\), evaluated between \(z\) and itself, equals \(-d_e\); consequently
\[
\lvert d_e\rvert\le\lVert\Delta_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{11}
\]
Since \(\lVert E\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=1\), equations (10)--(11) prove
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2M_n.
\tag{12}
\]
Trace duality now gives
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\lvert\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)\rvert
\le2n^{-2}\sup_B\lVert A_B\rVert_*M_n
\le2C_nM_n.
\tag{13}
\]
If \(nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\to0\), taking pilot expectations in (9) and (13) proves that both uniform errors are \(o(n^{-1})\).  Finally, (5) and (8) give
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\le4\underline\pi^{-1}K_M
\frac{n^{1+\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\tag{14}
\]
so \(\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}/n^{1+\beta}\to\infty\) is sufficient.  The derivation used only pilot sampling, bounded support, nonemptiness and regularity of the basis class, and the exposure-probability rate; neither known exposure nor a dependency graph entered. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility hold.  Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence holds, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
where \(C_n\) is exactly the deterministic sensitivity coefficient defined in lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate, and assume along the triangular sequence that
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Put also
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
Under \(nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\to0\),
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces.  Without it, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.  These selectors and limits are secondary regular rank-two deployment results.  No primitive condition in this theorem proves existence of uniformly bounded \(L_n\); the zero-surrogate first-order conclusion is conditional on the displayed global linear error bound.
statements.justification: This theorem derives nonempty measurable pilot selectors, finite pilot-selection regret, and a deterministic feasible-estimator variance bridge before taking the first-order limit.
statements.gap: The exact triangular-sequence sensitivity premise is explicit; the zero-surrogate first-order conclusion additionally requires a bounded deterministic linear error bound between nominal-gain regret and worst-loss deficit.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Put \(\mathcal K_n=\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\).  Assumption ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility makes \(\mathcal K_n\) nonempty.  Its normalized representatives form a closed subset of a product of two spheres, and the residual sign quotient is compact.  The uniform lower bound \(B^{\top}\Omega B\succeq n\kappa I_2\) makes matrix inversion continuous throughout this set.  Consequently both empirical criteria are continuous in the basis and Borel measurable in the finite pilot sample, and their optimizer sets are nonempty and compact.  The fixed signed-chart lexicographic selector is measurable: successively minimizing each coordinate over the preceding compact optimizer set gives a compact-valued graph, and each inverse image of a rational open interval can be expressed through infima over a fixed countable dense subset.  This proves the existence and measurability asserted in def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Assumption ass:known-exposure is inherited by the observable map, so the deployed outcome stack has the exposure-potential-outcome interpretation used below.

Let \(M_n,d_n,e_n\) be the displayed quantities in the theorem.  Lemma lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate gives, pathwise under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad
e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\tag{1}
\]
Choose \(B_n^\star\in\mathcal K_n\) with \(w(B_n^\star)=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}\).  Empirical optimality yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
&\le\widehat w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})+d_n\\
&\le\widehat w(B_n^\star)+d_n\\
&\le v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+2d_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
The population minimum gives the reverse inequality.  Taking pilot expectations and applying (1) proves
\[
0\le\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\tag{3}
\]

Conditional on the pilot, \(\widehat B_s\) is fixed and belongs to \(\mathcal K_n\).  Assumption ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence therefore permits application of lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence at this pilot-measurable basis.  Assumption ass:frechet-covariance-domain and thm:fixed-basis-endpoints give, for every fixed \(B\in\mathcal K_n\),
\[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(c_H)=w(B).
\tag{4}
\]
For two bounded real families, \(\lvert\sup_H f_H-\sup_H g_H\rvert\le\sup_H\lvert f_H-g_H\rvert\).  Apply this inequality to the uniform variance bridge in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, use (4), and then integrate over the pilot.  This proves
\[
\lvert V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)\rvert\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Under the explicit triangular-sequence hypothesis
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0,
\tag{6}
\]
equation (3) gives robust regret \(o(n^{-1})\).  Lemma lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence gives \(nR_n\to0\), so (3), (5), and (6) prove the two stated first-order conclusions for the robust selector and both feasible-estimator bridges.

For the zero-covariance selector, choose \(B_n^0\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}\), which is possible by compactness and continuity.  Empirical optimality and (1) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_n^\star-g_{\widehat B_0}(0)
&=g_{B_n^0}(0)-g_{\widehat B_0}(0)\\
&\le2e_n
\le4C_nM_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
If the displayed deterministic linear error bound holds, then
\[
[q_n-w(\widehat B_0)]_+
\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_{\widehat B_0}(0)\}
\le4L_nC_nM_n.
\tag{8}
\]
Since \(x\ge q-[q-x]_+\) for real \(x,q\), taking expectations in (8) proves
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\tag{9}
\]
If \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\), hypothesis (6) makes the right-hand side \(o(n^{-1})\), proving the stated consequence.  No primitive condition used above establishes such a uniformly bounded \(L_n\); (8)--(9) are explicitly conditional on that separate deterministic geometry.  Without it, (7) controls nominal-gain regret only and cannot supply a first-order worst-loss ordering.  All selectors remain in the regular rank-two class, where Zhao's pseudoinverse equals the ordinary inverse. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Assume ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and the conditions of thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer, including its exact hypothesis \(nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\to0\) and its deterministic linear error bound for the zero-surrogate argmax.  Suppose the attained ordinary-domain optimizer sets satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic and the sharpened pilot term.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.  Neither the optimizer-containment condition nor a primitive theorem yielding uniformly bounded \(L_n\) is proved here; both are separate checkable hypotheses.  The proposition concerns the positive-definite rank-two restriction only.
statements.justification: This proposition transfers an ordinary-domain population gap to a finite-pilot feasible-estimator variance gap using the sharpened pilot sensitivity.

statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Assumption ass:known-exposure gives the deployed estimator in def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator its exposure-potential-outcome interpretation.  Put
\[
v_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,Z}}w(B).
\]
The assumed optimizer containment implies
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=v_n,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\mathcal A_{0,Z},
\qquad
\Delta_Z=q_n-v_n.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, a global minimizer and every global zero-covariance maximizer are feasible in the smaller class.  Conversely, any smaller-class point attaining the corresponding global value belongs to the appropriate global optimizer set.

The robust-regret and zero-surrogate inequalities in thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer give
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
\ge\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\tag{2}
\]
Applying that theorem's feasible-estimator bridge once in each direction yields
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\tag{3}
\]
This establishes the finite end-to-end inequality.

Under the three displayed deterministic envelopes,
\[
C_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\le K_CK_M\frac{n^\beta}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}.
\tag{4}
\]
Substituting (4) and the bound on \(R_n\) into (3) gives
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge \Delta_Z
-(4L_n+2)K_CK_M\frac{n^\beta}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
-2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus the stated finite-\(n\) strictness condition makes the right-hand side positive and proves \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

For the asymptotic claim, multiply (3) by \(n\).  The explicitly retained premise
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0
\tag{6}
\]
and the assumed bound \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) imply
\[
n(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0.
\tag{7}
\]
Lemma lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence and \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\) give \(nR_n\to0\).  Hence (3) yields
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})
\ge\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0.
\]
The argument uses, rather than derives, optimizer containment, the bounded linear-error constants, and (6).  Every inner variance is conditional on the fixed potential-outcome array and is taken only over the known assignment law; the pilot and coupling expectations are ex ante evaluations.  The observable variance bridge remains confined to the positive-definite rank-two class. \(\square\)

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite network \(G\), known assignment law \(\nu\), known exposure maps \(f_i\), and two mutually exclusive exposure events.
sampling_model.units: The realized finite-population potential outcomes are fixed for design-based estimation; the i.i.d. law \(H\) is used only to choose the basis ex ante.
sampling_model.treatment: The main experiment draws \(W\sim\nu\), and assignment is the only randomness in the causal estimator conditional on the chosen basis.
sampling_model.overlap: Every exposure probability \(\pi_{i,a}\) is positive, and basis covariance is bounded below by \(\kappa\) on the optimization class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two arm-specific external or historical i.i.d. samples are mutually unpaired and independent of the later assignment; they estimate \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), while the cross-world copula is neither estimated nor assumed.

estimand_functional: Let \(r_\Omega=\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\), let \((C_k)_{k\ge1}\) enumerate the normalized rational-support classes of rank \(r_\Omega\), and set \(\rho_m=\inf_{k\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_k)=\inf_{[C]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(C)\), \(\widehat k_m=\min\{k\ge1:\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\}\), and \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}\) for finite \(\varepsilon_m>0\); moreover \(\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=(D_{i,1}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,1},-D_{i,0}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,0})_{i=1}^n\), \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)=S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}\).

tldr: Rare network exposures make Horvitz--Thompson estimation noisy, and Zhao's optimal indicator control variates reduce this design variance, but the ex ante basis depends on a cross-world covariance that an unpaired pilot cannot identify. The contribution chain imports the sharp Fréchet covariance range, proves a new fixed-basis affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's objective, poses certified global maximin optimization on the fixed-\(\kappa\) projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency without assuming away ties. Neighborhood persistence is supporting and witness-gated; no strict-dominance region is claimed unless the full-correspondence separation-and-slack certificate is produced.

project_justification.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates explicitly leaves robust basis choice under moment misspecification open; existing Fréchet results identify covariance endpoints, and existing global-optimization results certify Euclidean-box programs, but no paper joins these steps for a block-separable network basis with projective symmetry.
project_justification.niche: Two unpaired pilot marginals identify the exact dependence ambiguity relevant to Zhao's moment matrix while leaving the experimental network and assignment law fixed and known.
project_justification.fill: The project imports the sharp endpoint formulas, proves their affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, formulates a computably specified global maximin certificate on the compact \(\kappa\)-regular projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency. Conditional persistence is supporting: a strict-dominance region requires a separate certified witness with both separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack.

technical_internal_limitation: The presolve fractions \(521/1200\), \(2613/8432\), and \(4912/39525\) are not formal claims because the triangle exposure truth tables, the resulting entries of \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), the value of \(\kappa\), full equality-set bounds, and optimizer-wide strict \(\kappa\)-slack certificate are not supplied. The early kill test is oeq:separated-lawful-witness over exact assignment enumeration and both full optimizer correspondences. Unnumbered sanity check and regression test: if \(F_1\) and \(F_0\) are point masses, then the definitions give \(c_L=c_U=0\), hence \(r(B)=g_B(0)\) and \(\mathcal A_R=\mathcal A_0\). Zhao's Corollary 3 supports the stronger noiseless inverse-probability-weighted basis special case, while this correspondence equality is only a definitional code check and carries no theorem or novelty status.
honest_scope: The sharp Fréchet covariance range is imported from AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1. The new theorem targets are its affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, projective compactness, uniform plug-in value and outer-set consistency, and conditional neighborhood persistence. The finite epsilon-global solver and the separated lawful witness are first-class open constructions. Persistence is incremental and yields a strict-dominance region only after the witness supplies both a positive full-correspondence separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack; no such region is otherwise claimed. No SDP reduction, universal minimax interchange, universal strict improvement, asymptotic normality for the pilot-selected basis, or point convergence under ties is claimed.
